rulings.restated: Input — The year you placed this vehicle in service in the business (2019 to 2025; a vehicle placed in service earlier is outside this tool)
rulings.model: Column (b) instructions say "Enter the date the property was placed in service", but the restatement asks only for a year. The refusal for 50%-or-less use correctly sends that case to line 27, but the printed entry is still a year, not a date.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; restatement accepted. As line 43: the year chooses the recovery year and the limits, the quarter (asked separately) the mid-quarter table; the filer enters the full date on Form 4562 column (b).

rulings.restated: Input — The vehicle's cost (including sales tax) or other basis, not reduced by any section 179 deduction or depreciation
rulings.model: The restatement matches "actual cost (including sales tax) or other basis (unadjusted for prior years' depreciation)", but it leaves out the rule for converted vehicles: "If you converted the property from personal use to business/investment use, your basis for depreciation is the smaller of the property's adjusted basis or its fair market value on the date of conversion." The screen does not exclude conversions.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: fixed; restatement now matches. The cost question now says that for a vehicle converted from personal use the basis is the smaller of its adjusted basis or its fair market value on the date of conversion (i4562, Column (d)), as the property question already did.

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Placed in service in 2025" = true → helper "Line 19 for a 2025 vehicle, half-year or mid-quarter"] [helper "Placed in service in 2025" = false → helper "Line 19 for a vehicle placed in service before 2025 (zero after the recovery period, when the worksheet is not used)"]
rulings.model: The 2025 half-year and mid-quarter branches match "Multiply line 18 by line 6". But a 2019 vehicle (not refused) gets zero, and the instructions say "If the recovery period for an automobile ended before your tax year beginning in 2025, enter your unrecovered basis, if any, in column (h)", subject to the yearly limit (Pub. 946, Deductions After the Recovery Period). No refusal names this case.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; restatement accepted. Line 19 is a line of the automobile worksheet, which is not used after the recovery period; a 2019 vehicle's deduction is its unrecovered basis, limited and prorated (scveh.post, read by scveh.macrs_pass for column (h); Pub. 946 p. 61, Deductions After the Recovery Period), as stage14.veh.2019_cheap_mq3 asserts (BUG-0059).

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Leased and on actual expenses" = true → helper "The business portion of the lease payments"] [helper "Leased and on actual expenses" = false → helper "Zero"]
rulings.model: The restatement takes the business portion of the lease payments but leaves out the reduction the instructions require: "if you leased a vehicle for a term of 30 days or more, you may have to reduce your deduction by the inclusion amount." No refusal covers this case.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: refusal located elsewhere; restatement accepted. An inclusion amount for leased property is refused for the business through sc.special ('an inclusion amount for leased property'), so the business portion of the lease payments is the line 20a amount for every vehicle that reaches it.

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Leased and on actual expenses" = true → helper "The business portion of the lease payments"] [helper "Leased and on actual expenses" = false → helper "Zero"]

The instructions add: "But if you leased a vehicle for a term of 30 days or more, you may have to reduce your deduction by the inclusion amount." The restatement omits this reduction and has no refusal for it.

rulings.restated: Input — The year you first placed this vehicle in service for business purposes (for example 2023)
rulings.model: Schedule C line 43 asks for the full date: "When did you place your vehicle in service for business purposes? (month/day/year)". The restatement collects only the year (for example 2023).
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; restatement accepted. The tool needs the year (and, for 2025 property, the quarter) to choose the tables and limits; the filer writes the full date on Schedule C line 43 and Form 4562 from their own records. No value depends on the month or day except through the quarter, which is asked separately.

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Placed in service in 2025" = true → helper "Limit for a 2025 vehicle"] [helper "Placed in service in 2025" = false → helper "Limit for the vehicle's 2025 year of recovery"]
rulings.model: The 2025 amounts ($20,200 with the special allowance, $12,200 without) and the earlier-year amounts match the tables. But line 7 always applies the passenger-automobile limit, even when the filer says the vehicle is not a passenger automobile. The text says the limits apply "For any passenger automobile", and those vehicles have no refusal.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; restatement accepted. Line 7 is a line of the Pub. 946 worksheet for passenger automobiles and is shown for every vehicle, but it limits only a passenger automobile: for a vehicle that is not one, the special allowance, the section 179 deduction and MACRS take the scveh.passenger = false branches, which do not read it (checked: a $60,000 truck placed in service in 2025 with the 100% allowance gets $60,000, a passenger automobile $20,200).

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Placed in service in 2025" = true → helper "Limit for a 2025 vehicle"] [helper "Placed in service in 2025" = false → helper "Limit for the vehicle's 2025 year of recovery"]
rulings.model: The restatement applies the passenger-automobile table even when the vehicle is not a passenger automobile (scveh.passenger = false). The limit applies only "For any passenger automobile," and the text lists exceptions: "The following vehicles are not considered passenger automobiles." Through lines 9, 11, 17, 20 and 25, this caps depreciation on such vehicles. The table values themselves ($20,200, or $12,200 without the special allowance, for 2025) match.

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Standard mileage rate or actual expenses" = 'standard' → helper "Standard mileage amount plus parking fees and tolls"] [helper "Standard mileage rate or actual expenses" = 'actual' → helper "Business portion of the operating expenses plus parking fees and tolls"]
rulings.model: The standard branch matches ("Multiply the number of business miles driven by 0.70... Add to this amount your parking fees and tolls"). For actual expenses, the text says only "Include on line 9 the business portion of expenses for gasoline, oil, repairs, insurance, license plates, etc." It does not say whether parking fees and tolls are added in full under that method.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; restatement accepted. The parking input asks only for parking fees and tolls for the vehicle's business use, and Pub. 463 lists tolls and parking fees among actual car expenses (p. 21); being for business use only, they are added in full, as on the standard mileage rate branch.
